item.text:
**Assessment**
Kishida’s 2024 record looks **modestly positive but indirect** on `5B.2`: I found repeated use of formal economic councils, outside experts, and broad policy processes, but **little direct appointment evidence** proving that he selected top economic officials on merit rather than loyalty. I did **not** find credible 2024 evidence of family-member or business-partner appointments in economic posts.

**Positive**
1. **Meeting of the Council on Economic and Fiscal Policy** | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | July 29, 2024 | https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/actions/202407/29keizai.html | Kishida approved budget guidelines after medium- to long-term economic projections and said policy should deliver private-demand-led growth and income/wage increases above price rises. This is strong evidence of technocratic, institution-based economic management rather than patronage. | `5B.2`, `5B.1`
2. **Joint Meeting of the Council on Economic and Fiscal Policy and the Council of New Form of Capitalism Realization** | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | June 21, 2024 | https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/actions/202406/21keizai.html | Kishida advanced the 2024 revised “New Form of Capitalism” package and basic economic-management policy through formal councils, showing he was using structured policy institutions and experts to drive long-run growth and wage increases. | `5B.2`, `5B.1`
3. **Council of New Form of Capitalism Realization** | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | March 26, 2024 | https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/actions/202403/26shihon.html | The council discussed a shift from a demand-constrained to a growth-oriented economy, indicating Kishida continued to empower a formal economic-policy process oriented toward structural reform rather than short-term political gifts. | `5B.2`, `5B.1`
4. **GX 2040 Leaders Panel** | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | July 2, 2024 | https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/actions/202407/02gx_leaders.html | Kishida convened business leaders and energy/technology experts with cabinet members to design long-horizon energy and industrial strategy, a technocratic, non-nepotistic policy process. | `5B.2`, `5B.1`
5. **Ministerial Council on Acceptance and Inclusion of Foreign Human Resources** | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | February 9, 2024 | https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/actions/202402/09gaikoku.html | Kishida implemented an expert-panel report and told ministers to move forward with bills and labor-market reforms, which is evidence of relying on competence and institutional advice in a growth-relevant policy area. | `5B.2`, `5B.1`
6. **Council of New Form of Capitalism Realization** | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | April 17, 2024 | https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/actions/202404/17shihon.html | Kishida invited award-winning filmmakers as reference persons for contents-industry strategy, showing openness to sector experts and practical know-how rather than insider patronage. | `5B.2`

**Mixed / Negative**
1. **Embattled Japan PM faces ethics committee to save popularity and budget** | Reuters | February 28, 2024 | https://www.investing.com/news/economy/embattled-japan-pm-faces-ethics-committee-to-save-popularity-and-budget-3319362 | The funding scandal forced Kishida into defensive political management around popularity and the budget, which undercuts a pure technocratic reading and suggests short-term survival pressures were shaping his agenda. | `5B.2`, `5B.1`, `4B.10`
2. **Japan PM Kishida won’t run for reelection at LDP race** | Reuters | August 14, 2024 | https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/japan-pm-kishida-wont-run-for-reelection-at-ldp-race-kyodo-reports-3570455 | Reuters framed his exit as driven by scandal, weak approval, and living-cost anger; that is consistent with a leader reacting to political pressure more than steadily empowering an independent economic team. | `5B.2`, `4B.10`, `5B.1`
3. **Kishida compromised with conservative nationalists to stay in power** | Associated Press | September 30, 2024 | https://apnews.com/article/05926b50f4f5a83a631f779d906cf06d | AP described coalition bargaining with conservative nationalists to preserve office, which is mixed evidence: it does not show economic patronage, but it does show political survival bargaining that can dilute technocratic autonomy. | `5B.2`, `4B.10`

**Search Gap**
I did not find strong 2024 evidence that Kishida filled top economic posts with family members, business partners, or obvious loyalists, nor a clean appointment roster showing merit-based technocratic selection. The available evidence is mostly indirect: formal councils, expert panels, and policy outputs rather than personnel lists.
